regenerable_on: a lab guest with the exposure ruleset staged: the inet selab table (guarded jump to a bare accept, loopback blanket accept, an ipv6-icmp meta accept, an anonymous-set range dport accept, a negated udp dport with a source), plus one iptables-nft rule so the document carries a real xt residue. Every staged rule ACCEPTS and the base chain policy is accept, so staging cannot cut the guest's own ssh off.
note: port-exposure's first committed pair, staged so each closure discipline is reachable from a REAL capture rather than a fixture: the guard travels with the jump (the 2026-08-13 inversion), the meta-l4proto icmp accept is excluded from every tcp and udp socket, nft 1.1.6 spells an anonymous single-range set as a bare range object — which both implementations treat as an unreadable dport, possible and gapped — the negated dport is possible-never-certain, and the iptables-nft xt match is the live unreadable-clause shape, reaching only the v4 socket because it sits in an ip-family table. The same payload set carries listening (the join's other half) and the nft trio over a third distinct ruleset. One curation, the same one corpus/network/resolved states: the resolve1 manager document is staged minus DNSSECNegativeTrustAnchors — a compiled-in constant list identical on every install, read by neither implementation, whose reversed-octet in-addr.arpa spellings read as public addresses to any detector honest about address shapes.
coverage_note: What this variant does not reach: a prerouting/forward path (the PathCoverage statement is about exactly that), a drop that shadows a later accept (shadowing is listed, not resolved), and a verdict map dispatch — the vmap statement shape stays owned by the collector's unit tests until a staged ruleset carries one.
anchors_note: Each value hand-checked against the staged ruleset, over the SCRUBBED payloads. tcp 0.0.0.0:22 is certain from the loopback blanket and from the jump guard's subnet — the guard travelled, which is the inversion trap — and its gap names three rules: the bare-range dport (handle 6), the negated udp dport (7, which bears possibly on every socket the family reaches), and the xt rule (ip/filter/INPUT/2), which the tcp6 socket's gap list must NOT name because an ip-family table decides nothing about a v6 socket. The negated rule's staged source was 198.51.100.7; the scrubber's in-space substitution moved it to 192.0.2.144, and the anchor asserts the committed spelling. udp 127.0.0.53:53 shows possible wider than certain with no unreadable rendering involved on the certain side. nft-tables: two tables — the staged selab (six rules) and iptables-nft's ip filter.
